io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.implementation.listeners

Class VanillaContainerTitleListener

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.implementation.listeners.VanillaContainerTitleListener
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    org.bukkit.event.Listener

    public class VanillaContainerTitleListener
extends java.lang.Object
implements org.bukkit.event.Listener
    BlockListener.clearInheritedCustomName(org.bukkit.block.Block) clears a vanilla-container-backed SlimefunItem block's inherited CustomName on placement, so the GUI title is not frozen in the placer's language for every future viewer - but that leaves the block falling back to vanilla's own title (e.g. a placed Enhanced Furnace just reading "Furnace"). This retitles the just-opened vanilla Inventory for the opening viewer, to the block's Slimefun name (translated per viewer, the item id as the ultimate fallback), via one of two paths:
    • If PacketTranslationService.canRetitleWindows() - the packet layer can rewrite the open-window packet's title field before it ever reaches the client, so this hands the item id off to PacketTranslationService.notifyVanillaContainerOpen(org.bukkit.entity.Player, java.lang.String) and stops, with no visible flash at all.
    • Otherwise (older/newer server versions where that packet's title field could not be resolved reflectively), the one-tick-later InventoryView#setTitle correction below runs instead - the same mechanism BlockMenu.open(org.bukkit.entity.Player...) already applies to custom Slimefun GUIs, which still lets the wrong title flash for a frame.
